questions.question: How often are alert management rules checked by default in Event Management?

explanation.correct: Alert management rules are checked every 11 seconds by the default 'Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0' scheduled job. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 5 seconds is not the default interval
30 seconds is not the default interval
60 seconds is not the default interval

source.excerpt: Alert management rules are checked every 11 seconds by the default Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0 scheduled job.

questions.question: Which two roles can interact with Alert Management Rules? (Choose two.)

options.text: evt_mgmt_admin - can create and customize rules

explanation.correct: Users with the evt_mgmt_admin role can create and customize alert management rules. Users with the evt_mgmt_operator role can manually run alert management rules. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: itil role is not specifically mentioned for Alert Management Rules
evt_mgmt_user role capabilities don't include rule deletion

source.excerpt: Users with the evt_mgmt_admin role can use the alert management rule designer to create and customize alert management rules. Users with the evt_mgmt_operator role can manually run alert management rules.

questions.question: In which scenario will an alert management rule NOT execute?

options.text: When an open alert is updated
When a closed alert is updated
When alert severity changes from Warning to Major
When a new alert is created

explanation.correct: Alert management rules run on all updated open alerts. Rules don't run on closed alerts, even if they've been updated. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rules run on updated open alerts
Severity changes trigger rule evaluation if alert is open
New alerts trigger rule evaluation

source.excerpt: Alert management rules run on all updated open alerts. Rules don't run on closed alerts, even if they've been updated.

questions.question: Which three actions can be performed by Alert Management Rules? (Choose three.)

options.text: Launch a URL in a browser

explanation.correct: Alert Management Rules can specify responses including: run a subflow, open an incident, launch an application, or launch a URL in a browser. Events cannot be deleted by rules, and CMDB modifications are handled separately. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Events cannot be deleted by Alert Management Rules
CMDB relationships are managed separately, not by alert rules

source.excerpt: Actions: Specify the response to the alert, such as to run a subflow, perform remediation action, launch an application, or launch a URL in a browser.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for enhanced performance of Event Management scheduled jobs when performing alert remediation?

options.text: Disable all scheduled jobs and run manually
Increase the job interval to 60 seconds

explanation.correct: For enhanced performance of Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management scheduled jobs, use subflows instead of workflows. Subflows provide better performance characteristics. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Workflows are older technology; subflows are recommended for performance
Disabling jobs would prevent automatic processing
Increasing interval doesn't improve performance, just delays processing

source.excerpt: For enhanced performance of Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management scheduled jobs, use subflows instead of workflows.

questions.question: Which application package contains the Alert Management Rules functionality?

explanation.correct: Alert management rules are provided with the base system as a store application called Alert Rules Management [sn_em_arm]. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event Management is the parent application, but rules are in sn_em_arm
ITOM Core is the foundation, not the specific rules application
Service Analytics is for metrics, not alert rules

source.excerpt: Alert management rules provided with the base system as a store application (Alert Rules Management [sn_em_arm]) to help you respond to alerts.

questions.question: What is the purpose of creating Key Values for alert clustering?

options.text: To determine commonality between alerts and group them together
To create unique identifiers for each alert
To assign priority scores to alerts

explanation.correct: Key values create an additional way to determine commonality between alerts and to combine them into groups. For example, you may want to group alerts on CIs that share the same supplier or location. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/alert-clustering-cis.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Key values are for grouping, not encryption
Alert IDs are separate from clustering key values
Priority scoring is handled separately

source.excerpt: Key values create an additional way to determine commonality between alerts and to combine them into groups. For example, you may want to group alerts on CIs that share the same supplier or location.

questions.question: How can you prevent duplicate incident creation when both alert management and alert grouping jobs are running?

options.text: Synchronize alert response with automated alert grouping so management jobs run after grouping jobs
Run alert management jobs more frequently

explanation.correct: To avoid duplicate actions like incident creation on secondary alerts, synchronize alert response with grouping by ensuring alert management jobs run after alert grouping jobs complete. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Disabling grouping removes valuable functionality
Frequency increase doesn't prevent duplicates
Manual creation defeats automation purpose

source.excerpt: Synchronize alert response with grouping by ensuring alert management jobs runs after alert grouping jobs—this prevents duplicate actions like incident creation on secondary alerts.

questions.question: What is the name of the default scheduled job that evaluates Alert Management Rules?

options.text: Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0

explanation.correct: The default scheduled job that evaluates alert management rules is named 'Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0'. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is not the correct job name
This is not the correct job name
This is not the correct job name

source.excerpt: Alert management rules are checked every 11 seconds by the default Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0 scheduled job.

questions.question: Starting from which ServiceNow release do new users get two scheduled jobs for Alert Rules Management instead of one?

explanation.correct: Only new users from Vancouver and up get two scheduled jobs: Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0 and Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management1. Users upgrading from previous releases remain with a single job. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Tokyo predates the two-job configuration
Utah predates the two-job configuration
Washington DC is after Vancouver but the feature was introduced in Vancouver

source.excerpt: Only new users from Vancouver and up get two scheduled jobs: Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management0 and Event Management - Evaluate Scoped Alert Rules Management1.

questions.question: An organization has many alerts from CIs in the same datacenter. How can they configure Event Management to group these alerts together?

options.text: Create key values based on the CI's location attribute
Set all alerts to the same severity
Use the same event source for all CIs

explanation.correct: Key values can be created using CI attributes like location to determine commonality between alerts. For example, you may want to group alerts on CIs that share the same supplier or location. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/alert-clustering-cis.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Same severity doesn't create logical grouping
Event source alone doesn't enable location-based grouping
Identical message keys would merge alerts, not group them

source.excerpt: Key values create an additional way to determine commonality between alerts and to combine them into groups. For example, you may want to group alerts on CIs that share the same supplier or location.

questions.question: Which role is required to create key values for alert clustering?

explanation.correct: The evt_mgmt_admin role is required to create key values for alert clustering. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/alert-clustering-cis.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: itil is for ITSM tasks, not Event Management admin functions
evt_mgmt_user has limited permissions
cluster_admin is not a standard ServiceNow role

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Alert Management Rules are true?
a) Alert management rules can open incidents based on alert conditions
b) Rules run on closed alerts when they are updated
c) The alert execution history is automatically updated when actions are invoked
d) Rules can launch remediation actions on affected CIs

explanation.correct: Statements a, c, and d are true. Statement b is false - rules don't run on closed alerts, even if they've been updated. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement b is false - rules don't run on closed alerts
Statement d is also true about remediation actions
Statement b is false, not true

source.excerpt: Alert management rules run on all updated open alerts. Rules don't run on closed alerts. The alert's execution history is automatically updated to indicate the actions that were invoked.

questions.question: What happens to existing alert action rules from earlier releases when upgrading to a newer ServiceNow version?

options.text: They can be executed but cannot be modified until migrated
They continue to work without any changes needed
They are automatically converted to subflows

explanation.correct: Existing alert action rules from an earlier release can be executed, but cannot be modified. Alert action rules that have been migrated become alert management rules and all definitions are migrated to the new format. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Old rules are retained, not deleted
Modification requires migration to the new format
Rules migrate to alert management rules, not subflows

source.excerpt: Existing alert action rules from an earlier release can be executed, but cannot be modified. Alert action rules that have been migrated become alert management rules.

questions.question: An administrator wants to configure a rule that sends an email when alert severity changes to Major. How should the filter be configured?

options.text: No filter needed - rules apply to all alerts
Filter condition specifying severity equals Major
Use Related List Conditions with severity history
Create a separate rule for each severity level

explanation.correct: Filters ensure that the rule is invoked only when the configured condition occurs. A filter condition can specify that the alert management rule runs only when the alert severity is critical (or Major in this case). Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Without filters, the rule would run on every update
Related List Conditions are for related record filtering, not severity
Multiple rules are not needed; one filtered rule is sufficient

source.excerpt: Filters ensure that the rule is invoked only when the configured condition occurs. A filter condition can specify that the alert management rule runs only when the alert severity is critical.

questions.question: What type of information can be configured in the Related List Conditions section of an Alert Management Rule?

options.text: Conditions based on related records, such as alerts received today with a Parent relationship
LDAP group membership for assignment routing

explanation.correct: In the Related List Conditions section, you can configure additional conditions with relationships. For example, with an Alert > Parent relationship, you can filter for any alerts that were received today. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: LDAP integration is separate from Alert Management Rules
Email templates are configured in notifications, not rule conditions
Scheduled job timing is configured in the job, not rule conditions

source.excerpt: In the Related List Conditions section of the form, configure additional conditions, for example, with an Alert > Parent relationship, to filter for any alerts that were received today.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for large-scale environments that need to process alert management rules faster?

options.text: Decrease the job interval to 5 seconds
Add more scheduled jobs by contacting Customer Service and Support
Upgrade to a higher ServiceNow instance tier
Disable half of the alert management rules

explanation.correct: For large-scale environments, you can add more than one scheduled job to process alert management rules. This requires contacting Customer Service and Support. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Modifying the interval is not recommended without guidance
Instance tier doesn't directly address job processing
Disabling rules removes functionality

source.excerpt: For large-scale environments, you can add more than one job. Please contact Customer Service and Support.

questions.question: Which property should NOT be modified according to ServiceNow documentation regarding Alert Rules Management scheduled jobs?

explanation.correct: ServiceNow documentation explicitly warns: Don't modify the sn_em_arm.alert_management.num_of_jobs property. Changes should be made through Customer Service and Support. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property is not specifically mentioned as restricted
This property is not specifically mentioned as restricted
This property is not specifically mentioned as restricted

questions.question: What are the three types of categories that determine the alert priority score?

options.text: Accumulated categories, choice-list categories, and time-based categories
Accumulated categories, choice-list categories, and CI type weight factor mapping
Static categories, dynamic categories, and CI type categories
Severity categories, impact categories, and urgency categories

explanation.correct: The alert priority score is a composite of accumulated categories (e.g., number of impacted business services, CI type, number of secondary alerts), choice-list categories (alert state, severity, role), and CI type weight factor mapping. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-priority.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no 'time-based categories' concept in alert priority scoring.
Static and dynamic categories are not the terminology used for alert priority.
These are ITIL incident priority factors, not Event Management alert priority categories.

questions.question: In rule-based alert grouping, what happens when a secondary alert has its own secondary alert?

options.text: The hierarchy is flattened to preserve only two levels
The deepest secondary alert is removed from the group
Both secondary alerts become primary alerts

explanation.correct: Only one level of secondary alerts is permitted. Event Management flattens the hierarchy to preserve only two levels - a primary alert and sibling secondary alerts. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventCorrelationRules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event Management does not allow more than two levels in alert correlation hierarchies.
The alert is not removed; instead, it becomes a sibling secondary alert under the original primary.
Secondary alerts do not become primary alerts through hierarchy flattening.

questions.question: An administrator sets the property evt_mgmt.rule_based_manual_closure to 'No'. What happens when the primary alert is closed?

options.text: Secondary alerts remain grouped under the primary alert
Secondary alerts become stand-alone open alerts
The parent reference is removed and secondary alerts are closed
Secondary alerts are automatically escalated to incidents

explanation.correct: When the property is set to No, after the primary alert is closed, the parent reference is removed from the secondary alerts (grouping is dissolved), and the secondary alerts are closed and become stand-alone. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventCorrelationRules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The grouping is always dissolved when the primary alert is closed.
This behavior occurs when the property is set to Yes, not No.
Secondary alerts are not automatically escalated to incidents when a primary closes.

questions.question: Which property determines how Event Management handles a new event similar to events on an existing closed alert?

explanation.correct: The active interval property (evt_mgmt.active_interval) determines whether a new event reopens an existing closed alert or creates a new alert. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMAlertRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property controls whether reopening an alert also reopens associated incidents.
This property controls whether resolving an incident also closes the alert.
This is not a real Event Management property name.

questions.question: When a CI is in maintenance due to an active change request, how are alerts on that CI treated in Event Management?

options.text: Alerts are deleted from the system
Alerts are excluded from impact calculation and hidden from the Alerts tab
Alerts continue to appear normally but are marked as low priority

explanation.correct: When a CI is in maintenance, all alerts on the affected CI are excluded from impact calculation, and the Alerts tab temporarily hides all corresponding alerts. The impact tree shows the CI in green with a note of '(In Maintenance)'. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMHowImpactTree.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alerts are not deleted; they are temporarily hidden and excluded from impact calculation.
Alerts are not resolved; they are hidden until maintenance ends.
Alerts are hidden, not just marked as low priority.

questions.question: Which of the following is an accumulated category in the alert priority score calculation?

explanation.correct: Number of secondary alerts is an accumulated category. A parent alert with many secondary alerts has a higher priority than one with fewer. Alert state, severity, and role are choice-list categories. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-priority.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alert state is a choice-list category, not an accumulated category.
Alert severity is a choice-list category, not an accumulated category.
Role is a choice-list category, not an accumulated category.

questions.question: An alert has severity Critical and is the parent of 15 secondary alerts impacting 3 business services. Which factor does NOT contribute to its priority score?

options.text: The description text of the alert

explanation.correct: The alert description text is not a factor in priority score calculation. Priority is determined by accumulated categories (impacted services, CI type, secondary alerts) and choice-list categories (state, severity, role). Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-priority.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Number of impacted business services is an accumulated category that contributes to the priority score.
Number of secondary alerts is an accumulated category that contributes to the priority score.
Alert severity is a choice-list category that contributes to the priority score.

questions.question: Three alert correlation rules exist: Rule 1 makes A secondary to B, Rule 2 makes C and D secondary to A, and Rule 3 makes A secondary to E. When all alerts trigger, what is the final grouping?

options.text: E is primary with A, B, C, D as secondary alerts
B is primary with A, C, D as secondary alerts; E is standalone
A is primary with B, C, D, E as secondary alerts
B and E are both primary alerts for A

explanation.correct: Rule 1 makes A secondary to B. Rule 2 makes C and D secondary to A, but the hierarchy is flattened so A, C, D are all secondary to B. Rule 3 cannot apply because multiple parents are not allowed (A already has B as primary). E remains standalone. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventCorrelationRules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rule 3 cannot override Rule 1 since A already has B as its primary. Multiple parents are not allowed.
Rule 1 executes first, making A secondary to B, not a primary alert.
Multiple parents are not allowed in Event Management alert correlation.

questions.question: What happens when you resolve an incident that is associated with an alert?

options.text: The alert is always automatically closed
The alert can close based on the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property
The alert state changes to Acknowledged
The alert is moved to a historical table

explanation.correct: When you resolve an incident associated with an alert, the alert can also close according to the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property setting. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMAlert.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The behavior depends on the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property; it is not always automatic.
Resolving an incident does not change the alert to Acknowledged state.
Alerts are not moved to a historical table when incidents are resolved.

questions.question: Which alert group type can be configured using the Automatic Group Filter?

explanation.correct: The Automatic Group Filter supports three group types: Automated, CMDB, and Text. You can assign more than one group type with a single filter condition, but each group type can have only one active filter. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/alert-filtering.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual alert grouping is not configured through Automatic Group Filters.
Rule-based is not one of the group types for Automatic Group Filters; Text is also supported.
Time-based is not a valid group type. The correct types are Automated, CMDB, and Text.

questions.question: A change request for a CI has a state of 'Scheduled' and the current time is between the Planned start date and Planned end date. How does Event Management treat this CI?

options.text: The CI and its alerts are treated normally
The CI is considered in maintenance; alerts are excluded from impact calculation
Only critical alerts on the CI are shown
The CI is removed from the CMDB temporarily

explanation.correct: An active change request has State = Scheduled or Implement AND the current time is between planned/actual start and end dates. The CI is considered in maintenance and alerts are excluded from impact calculation. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMHowImpactTree.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: When a change request is active and within the scheduled time window, the CI is in maintenance.
All alerts are hidden, not just non-critical ones.
The CI remains in the CMDB; it is simply treated as being in maintenance.

questions.question: What is the default value mapping for the 'Open' alert state in the alert priority score?

explanation.correct: In the alert priority score, the default mapping values for alert states are: Open = 1, Reopen = 2, Flapping = 3. Priority is not calculated for Closed state. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-priority.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 0 is not a default state mapping value. Open defaults to 1.
2 is the default mapping value for Reopen state, not Open.
3 is the default mapping value for Flapping state, not Open.
